  "insights": [
   "Rebecca Cheong (UBS Sales and Trading, not UBS Research) keeps a medium-term bullish view on U.S. equities despite the recent Hedge Fund and Systematic unwinds.",
   "The main structural change in U.S. equity markets over 15 years is the growing weight of long-duration capital (Retail Investors, Retirement Assets, Foreign Investors) next to fast growth in short-duration trading capital (Systematic, Quantitative, Hedge Fund strategies).",
   "Long-duration capital increasingly drives market trends and short-duration capital increasingly drives volatility. Corrections have become more frequent and sharper, and recoveries faster and more persistent.",
   "Short-term volatility and long-term direction are treated as separate forces. Unless the drivers of capital persistence deteriorate meaningfully, systematic deleveraging is more likely to create temporary dislocations than durable changes to the long-term trend.",

  "insights": [
   "JPM's economists expect the fed funds rate to go from 4.00% to 4.25% in December and then hold. The 10-year yield is around the ~5.00% near-term expectation, and the report cites a 5.24% 10-year in the utilities section.",
   "Equity strategy base case is a shallow hiking cycle, a reversal of last year's insurance cuts, which equities can absorb given the earnings anchor. A broader cycle of four to five hikes would likely cause more significant downside and is not the base case.",
   "Over the past year expectations moved from cuts to hikes. Long-dated Treasuries are down about 7% and forward P/E has compressed by about 3x, but equities are still up 12% YTD on earnings growth of 28% for 2026 and 22% for 2027.",
   "The US 30-year yield is about 5.35%, near 20-year highs. JPM attributes the back-end selloff to central bank repricing, sticky inflation from oil and trade shocks, rising fiscal deficits, and possible crowding out as foreign investors shift toward corporate debt (LTM $403B vs ~$397B for Treasuries).",
   "Roughly 80 years of data show an inverted U between the 10-year yield and S&P 500 multiples. With above-trend EPS growth (~15% y/y) yields can rise to ~5% before multiples de-rate. With consensus forward EPS growth above 20% and the S&P at ~18x 2027 EPS, JPM says equities could withstand a 10-year yield of ~5.5-6.0%.",
   "Primary risk named is further geopolitical escalation in the Middle East creating a more severe inflation and growth shock. Other risks are weaker earnings growth and an abrupt, volatile bond selloff.",
   "First-order effect on corporate interest expense should be gradual because debt is mostly fixed and long-dated. Financials' higher profitability and returns on ~$2.4T of cash offset it near term. Pressure concentrates in lower-income consumers, smaller companies, highly leveraged firms and capital-intensive industries outside the AI buildout.",
   "Sector leadership depends on curve shape. Bear steepeners have favored Cyclicals such as Energy and Financials, bear flatteners have favored Technology, and bond proxies and long-duration sectors ex-Technology (Utilities, Real Estate, Comm Services, Staples) are most exposed. Base case keeps JPM in Growth and Quality Growth with large caps over small caps. A broader hiking cycle would argue for rotation into Low Vol.",
   "JPM launched three thematic baskets: Beneficiaries of Higher Rates (JPRHIRTB), Beneficiaries of Lower Rates (JPRLORTB) and Agnostic Beneficiaries (JPRAGRTB). Performance lookback chart shows the baskets at 93.7, 69.7 and 97.1 rebased to 100 (labels not mapped to values in the text).",
   "Higher-rate beneficiaries are asset-sensitive banks, BDCs, insurers, payroll and HSA float earners, net-cash restaurants and media, integrated oils, auto-parts retailers, waste services, EDA software, custom silicon and process control.",
   "Large banks: higher rates are positive for NII through lagged deposit repricing, with a modest, manageable hit to capital from HTM and AFS marks. BAC is the more asset-sensitive pick, C benefits from non-US rates, and TFC is relatively disadvantaged by its swap book. JPM sees no 2023-style crisis risk in its universe.",
   "BDCs: ARCC is JPM's preferred way to play higher rates, followed by BXSL. Both trade near 1.0x NAV vs 0.60-0.70x for most peers and kept their dividends. Commercial mortgage REITs (ABR, KREF) face non-accrual and resolution drag.",
   "Insurers benefit from higher investment income. Commercial lines have net investment income of up to ~60% of earnings, reinsurers 40-60%, personal lines under 40%.",

   "AI infrastructure builders are the most rate-exposed in tech and communications. CoreWeave has ~8-9% cost of debt, Oracle has net cash capex of ~$70B dependent on external funding, and IREN expects $25-30B of FY27 capex.   "insights": [
   "The Fed held its policy rate at 3.75-4.0 percent, as expected by the market, by Handelsbanken's forecast and by the economist consensus.",
   "The decision was not unanimous. Two FOMC members dissented in favour of a hike, whereas September's decision was unanimous.",
   "Fed chair Kevin Warsh's communication was read as unexpectedly dovish. The FOMC wants an 'accumulation of more information' before any policy change, and Warsh was uncommitted to the rate hike that FOMC colleagues have signalled as appropriate this year.",
   "The market reaction was yield curve steepening (lower front end, higher long end) and a weaker dollar. Handelsbanken expects a string of FOMC members to try to walk back this move.",
   "Handelsbanken compares the communication to the July FOMC meeting delivery, which it calls disastrous, and sees increased risk of a dovish policy mistake.",
   "Handelsbanken argues that underlying inflation is set to resurge, based on leading indicators, after a period when many gauges showed progress toward the 2 percent target.",
   "Handelsbanken criticizes Warsh for three things: appearing unaware of leading indicator signals, saying he does not know whether strong supply- and demand-driven US growth is contributing to inflation, and being too relaxed about inflation expectations, which many measures show are high and rising.",
   "Handelsbanken keeps its call for a December rate hike and forecasts healthy GDP growth and a strengthening labour market.",
   "Warsh said he is 'unable and unwilling' to call current financial conditions 'tight'. Handelsbanken agrees conditions are not tight and expects the FOMC majority to conclude it has more work to do.",
   "Handelsbanken says financial conditions may improve again after the midterm elections, a common pattern, and if the US-Iran war moves closer to its end.",
   "The Fed will reduce its number of policy meetings. From next autumn one scheduled FOMC meeting will be reserved for strategy and major economic issues review with no policy decision. A second such meeting is added in 2028, giving 7 policy meetings in 2027 and 6 in 2028.",

 {
  "source": "ZeroHedge",
  "title": "\"The Age Of Idiosyncratic Risk\": BofA Says Options Are Underpricing Megacap Earnings Blowups, While Europe Overpays",
  "type": "derivatives",
  "priority": "high",
  "published": "2026-10-29",
  "insights": [
   "BofA's Global Equity Volatility Insights note (team led by Benjamin Bowler) finds single-stock fragility remains a defining feature of equity markets into year-end, even with index vol subdued.",
   "3-month ATM weighted-average stock vol is 38% for the SPX Top 50, about 2.5x the equivalent index vol, and 31% in Europe, about 1.8x the SX5E.",
   "BofA's conclusion is that US earnings vol is still cheap and European earnings vol is rich. The US earnings vol premium has risen, but realised moves have risen more, with the underpricing most pronounced in megacaps.",
   "Europe shows the opposite pattern: implied earnings risk is near historical extremes, yet only about a third of stocks have recently moved more than options implied.",
   "BofA defines 'fragility events' as days when a stock moves more than 3 sigma relative to its trailing 21-day vol. Last year set a record in Europe and 2026 is tracking close pro-rata, on course for one of Europe's top five years.",
   "BofA measures earnings pricing by comparing 'excess' implied vol around each earnings date (the expiry containing the release versus an interpolated no-earnings fair value) with the excess vol that subsequently realises.",
   "For the equal-weighted SPX Top 50, the implied earnings premium is at its 85th percentile and the realised premium is at its 91st.",
   "Market-cap weighting widens the US gap: realised earnings vol for the index-weighted SPX Top 50 is at its 100th percentile versus the 77th for implied, so the bigger the company, the bigger the underpricing.",
   "The US implied earnings premium has grown in absolute vol points (85th percentile) but not as a share of total stock variance (51st percentile). Options are pricing more earnings risk mostly because they price more risk overall.",
   "More than half of SPX Top 50 names by count, and more than two-thirds by market cap, have recently realised bigger earnings moves than options implied. The weighted reading is in its 98th percentile.",
   "In August BofA flagged that all six Mag7 stocks that had reported realised moves far greater than implied, a first in the ChatGPT era. The options market has not caught up since.",
   "In Europe, excess vol priced around earnings is at its 94th percentile for equal-weighted SX5E names, while realised is at the 78th. Index-weighted, implied is at the 94th percentile and realised at the 72nd, so the richness is not a function of company size.",
   "Normalised for stock vol level, European earnings risk as a share of total variance is at its 74th percentile.",
   "Only about a third of European stocks, and a similarly low share by market cap, have recently moved more on earnings than options anticipated, a 33rd percentile reading on both measures.",
   "BofA's trade conclusion: own US single-stock earnings optionality, particularly in megacaps where underpricing is most extreme, and sell (or be a very reluctant buyer of) European earnings vol."
